Tomitaro Makino (牧野 富太郎, Makino Tomitarō; 24 April 1862 – 18 January 1957) was a pioneer Japanese botanist noted for his taxonomic work.
In what year was Aluminium discovered?
Aluminium (the Commonwealth and preferred IUPAC name) or aluminum (North American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Al and atomic number 13.
Which company manufactures Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: Skunk Works. The SR-71 was developed in the 1960s as a black project by Lockheed's Skunk Works division.
Cro-Magnon: France. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Tucana?
Tucana: Petrus Plancius. Tucana (The Toucan) is a constellation in the southern sky, named after the toucan, a South American bird.
Who is credited with discovering Cro-Magnon?
Cro-Magnon: Louis Lartet. Cro-Magnons produced Upper Palaeolithic cultures, the first major one being the Aurignacian, which was succeeded by the Gravettian by 30,000 years ago.
Who is credited with discovering Makemake?
Makemake: Michael E. Brown. Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this family of hook-billed raptors includes buzzards, vultures, and kites across 75 genera — which family is this?
Accipitridae is one of the four families within the order Accipitriformes, and is a family of small to large birds of prey with strongly hooked bills and variable morphology based on diet.
A close relative of the peach in the genus Prunus, this drupe's seed isn't a true nut and can be "blanched" by softening its skin in hot water before peeling — what is it?
This British-American theoretical physicist at the University of Illinois reshaped our understanding of superfluid helium, work crowned by the 2003 Nobel Prize in Physics — who was he?
Anthony Leggett (26 March 1938 - 8 March 2026) was a British-American theoretical physicist and professor at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC).
This common long-term inflammatory airway disease causes wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath that can flare into sudden attacks triggered by allergens or pollen. What condition is it?
Asthma is a common long-term inflammatory disease of the airways. It is characterized by variable and recurring symptoms and reduced lung function.
Strawberries, blackcurrants and blueberries all count in the kitchen sense — though botanists would object, since the culinary meaning of this word differs from the scientific one. What word?
Berry is a small, pulpy, and often edible fruit.

Developed in Germany from the Old English Bulldog and the now-extinct Bullenbeisser, this medium-to-large mastiff-type dog breed is known for its square muzzle, underbite, and powerful bite — name the breed?
Boxer (dog breed) is a medium to large, short-haired dog breed of mastiff-type, developed in Germany.
The leaves and buds of this evergreen shrub, when processed differently, yield green, black, oolong, white, and yellow varieties of the world's most popular hot beverage — what's the species?
Camellia sinensis is a species of evergreen shrub or small tree in the flowering plant family Theaceae.
In calculus, this formula lets you find the derivative of a composed function h(x) = z(y(x)) using the derivatives of z and y separately — what is it called?
Chain rule is a formula that expresses the derivative of the composition of two differentiable functions z and y in terms of the derivatives of z and y.
Living in a symbiotic partnership with sea anemones that shelter them from predators, these Indo-Pacific reef fish live in groups led by a dominant breeding female. What fish are they?
Clownfish (genus Amphiprion) are saltwater fish found in the warm and tropical waters of the Indo-Pacific.
Which genus of passerine birds, whose Latin name literally means 'raven,' includes about 46 species commonly known as crows, ravens, and rooks?
Corvus is a widely distributed genus of passerine birds ranging from medium-sized to large-sized in the family Corvidae.
Used to treat ADHD and narcolepsy, this 'right-handed' mirror-image form of a stimulant molecule is also misused to boost cognitive and athletic performance — what is it?
Dextroamphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant and enantiomer of amphetamine that is used in the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy.
Long used in traditional Indigenous medicine, this prairie-dwelling genus of purple daisy relatives gets its name from a Greek word meaning 'hedgehog' — what plant is it?
Echinacea is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants in the daisy family.

Discovered in January 2005 by a Palomar Observatory team and named after a Greco-Roman goddess of strife, this trans-Neptunian object is the most massive known dwarf planet in the solar system — which one?
Eris (dwarf planet) (minor-planet number 136199) is the most massive and second-largest known dwarf planet in the Solar System.
With over two hundred species across fifty genera, this bird family includes canaries, siskins, redpolls, grosbeaks, and the Hawaiian honeycreepers — which family of seed-eating passerines?
Finch are small to medium-sized passerine birds in the family Fringillidae.
Caused by abnormalities in the genome, this category of health problem may arise from a single faulty gene, many genes, or a chromosome abnormality — what is the general term?
Genetic disorder is a health problem caused by one or more abnormalities in the genome.
Nicknamed the 'benevolent dictator for life' of the language he invented, this Dutch programmer relinquished that title in July 2018. Who is he?
Guido van Rossum (born 31 January 1956) is a Dutch programmer.
This genus of the mallow family includes several hundred species prized for their large, showy blooms, and is sometimes known by the alternate name rose mallow — name the genus?
Hibiscus is a genus of common flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae.
Prized in folk medicine as an antiseptic and expectorant, this Lamiaceae shrub grows wild from Southern Europe to the Caspian Sea area — which plant is it?
Hyssopus officinalis is a shrub in the Lamiaceae or mint family native to Southern Europe, the Middle East, and the region surrounding the Caspian Sea.
This Canadian-American physical educator invented an entire sport, wrote its original rule book after moving to the United States, and founded the University of Kansas's program in 1898 — who is he?
James Naismith (November 6, 1861 - November 28, 1939) was a Canadian-American physical educator, physician, Christian chaplain, and sports coach, best known as the inventor of the game of basketball.
Cousin to the wallaby and wallaroo in the family Macropodidae, this Australian marsupial's biggest member is the red one. What is it?
Kangaroo are marsupials from the subfamily Macropodinae (macropods, meaning "large foot").

Which citrus-scented perennial herb in the mint family, whose genus name Melissa comes from the Greek for 'honey bee,' is naturalized worldwide after originating in the Mediterranean and Central Asia?
Lemon balm (Melissa officinalis) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the mint family.
This Berkeley professor upended classical logic by proposing 'fuzzy' mathematics — fuzzy sets, fuzzy logic, fuzzy control, and more — who was he?

Lotfi A. Zadeh (4 February 1921 - 6 September 2017) was a mathematician, computer scientist, electrical engineer, artificial intelligence researcher, and professor of computer science at the University of California, Berkeley.
Sharing the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on nuclear shell structure, this German-American theorist became only the second woman ever to win that prize, after Marie Curie — who was she?
Maria Goeppert Mayer (ne Goppert; June 28, 1906 - February 20, 1972) was a German-American theoretical physicist who shared the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physics with J. Hans D. Jensen.
This branch of economics studies how individuals and firms allocate scarce resources within individual markets, as opposed to the economy as a whole — what field is it?

Microeconomics is a branch of economics that studies the behavior of individuals and firms in making decisions regarding the allocation of scarce resources and the interactions among these individuals and firms.
This semiaquatic rodent can stay submerged for up to seventeen minutes, propelled mainly by its webbed hind feet while its long, scaly tail helps steer — what animal is it?
Muskrat (Ondatra zibethicus) is a medium-sized semiaquatic rodent.
A reddish-brown gas that's a key step in making nitric acid for fertilizer, it also seeps into homes from gas-stove cooking and harms indoor air — which compound, formula NO2?
Nitrogen dioxide is a chemical compound with the formula NO2.

This group of middle-ear inflammations includes a painful acute infection that makes young children tug at their ears, plus a quieter form defined by non-infectious fluid lingering for weeks. What is the condition?
Otitis media is a group of inflammatory diseases of the middle ear.
Built for the sea, it sports a spiny tongue and powerful jaws to grip slippery fish, then swallows them whole mid-swim. Which animal splits its life half on land, half in the water?
Penguin are a group of flightless semi-aquatic sea birds which live almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere.
Native to South America and the most economically important member of the Bromeliaceae family, this tropical 'multiple fruit' became a 17th-century European symbol of luxury — what is it?
Pineapple (Ananas comosus) is a tropical plant with an edible fruit; it is the most economically significant plant in the family Bromeliaceae.

This male sexual dysfunction occurs when orgasm happens very soon after minimal sexual stimulation, with medical experts generally setting the threshold at around one minute — what's this condition called?

Premature ejaculation (PE) is a male sexual dysfunction that occurs when a male expels semen (and most likely experiences orgasm) soon after beginning sexual activity, and with minimal penile stimulation.
This colorless, odorless radioactive noble gas has the atomic number 86, and its longest-lived isotope has a half-life of under four days — name the element?
Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
Known by the common name 'dog rose,' this climbing wild rose species is native across Europe and stretches into northwest Africa and western Asia — which species?
Rosa canina is a variable climbing, wild rose species native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia.

Seven living species make up this group of ocean-dwelling reptiles, five of which are threatened with extinction — one species, found only near Australia, Papua New Guinea, and Indonesia, is not — name this group?
Sea turtle (superfamily Chelonioidea), sometimes called marine turtles, are reptiles of the order Testudines and of the suborder Cryptodira.
Whether on land, in fresh water, or in the sea, this gastropod earns its name from a coiled shell roomy enough to fully retract into — what is it?
Snail is a shelled gastropod. The name is most often applied to land snails, terrestrial pulmonate gastropod molluscs.
This group of cartilaginous fish spans eleven families and roughly 220 species, from tiny river-dwellers to giant manta and devil rays — what group of fish is it?
Stingray are a group of rays, a type of cartilaginous fish.
This fibrous connective tissue connects muscle to bone, unlike its cousin which connects bone to bone, and numbers about 4,000 throughout the adult human body — what is it?
Tendon is a tough band of dense fibrous connective tissue that connects muscle to bone.
Caused by superantigens from staph or strep bacteria, this condition brings fever, a sunburn-like rash, and peeling skin, and has been tied to absorbent tampon use — which condition?
Toxic shock syndrome (TSS) is a condition caused by bacterial toxins.
This abnormal enlargement of the vein network draining the testicles is the most common correctable cause of male infertility, found in over a third of men with the condition. Name it?
Varicocele is an abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform venous plexus in the scrotum.
This biological process unfolds in predictable phases — hemostasis, inflammation, cell proliferation, and tissue remodeling — to replace damaged skin after the barrier is broken. What is it?
Wound healing refers to a living organism's replacement of destroyed or damaged tissue by newly produced tissue.
Unearthed in Montana by Jack Horner's team in 1987, this 20-foot horned dinosaur sported a bony neck-frill and lived roughly 75 million years ago — which species?
Achelousaurus: Genus of ceratopsid dinosaur from North America.
Often called the father of theoretical computer science, this Englishman gave us a famous 'machine' that formalized the very idea of computation — who was he?
Nicknamed 'whip-spiders' or 'tailless whip-scorpions,' these arachnids have no silk, no venom, and a name meaning 'blunt tail' — they grab with their pedipalps instead of biting — what order is this?
Amblypygi: Order of arachnids. The name "amblypygid" means "blunt tail", a reference to a lack of the flagellum that is otherwise seen in whip-scorpions.

Named from Greek words meaning "unlike other shrimp," this extinct arthropod from the Burgess Shale had swimming flaps, big compound eyes and grasping frontal appendages, reaching over a foot long — which prehistoric predator?
Anomalocaris: Extinct genus of cambrian radiodont.

Nicknamed for its resemblance to a stinging insect, this orb-weaver spider sports bold yellow, white, and black bands across Central and Northern Europe, parts of Asia and Africa, and even the Azores — what species is it?
Argiope bruennichi: Species of orb-weaver spider. Like many other members of the same genus Argiope, this species has distinctive yellow, white and black markings on its abdomen.
Native to tropical Southeast Asia, this small tree bears bell-shaped rose-to-purple flowers and a ridged fruit that forms star-shaped slices when cut crosswise — which species?
Averrhoa carambola: Species of tree. It is a small tree or shrub that grows 5 to 12 m (16 to 39 ft) tall, with rose to red-purple flowers.

When no one else had the staff for it, this American lawyer volunteered to prosecute the Einsatzgruppen trial at Nuremberg, then spent decades championing an International Criminal Court — who was he?

In this distributed ledger, each record holds a cryptographic hash of the one before it, so altering a single block would require rewriting every block that follows — making the data nearly tamper-proof. What is it?
Blockchain: Distributed data store for digital transactions.
This plant family — nicknamed the mustards or crucifers, and including cabbage — hosts the caterpillars of a notorious garden-pest butterfly as one of its worst enemies — name the family?
Native to tropical Africa, this gourd-producing vine yields fruit that can be eaten young as a vegetable or dried and hollowed out into bowls, ladles, or even musical instruments — what is it?
Calabash: Species of bottle gourd plant.
Ranked the world's richest person by Forbes from 2010 to 2013, this Mexican tycoon built his fortune largely through telecommunications and remains Latin America's wealthiest individual — who is he?
Around 20 millimetres long with a shimmering structural-green shell and a coppery underside, this beetle is identified by its isosceles-triangle scutellum — which species?
Cetonia aurata: Species of beetle. The scutellum is the small V-shaped area between the wing cases; it may show several small, irregular, white lines and marks.
This plant genus includes both chicory, whose roasted roots make a coffee substitute, and true endive, the base for salad greens like escarole — which genus?
Cichorium: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae.
Named for an Indonesian island where an 18th-century naturalist first catalogued it, this pungent, oregano-scented succulent also goes by Cuban oregano and Indian borage — which plant?
Coleus amboinicus: Species of plant. Coleus amboinicus is a species of semi-succulent perennial plant in the family Lamiaceae.
Latin for 'raven,' this widely distributed bird genus includes crows and rooks and gave a group of its members the eerie collective noun 'a murder' — what genus is it?
Corvus: Genus of birds including crows, ravens and rooks.

First synthesized in 1874, this insecticide earned its discoverer a 1948 Nobel Prize and was used in WWII against malaria and typhus before becoming infamous for its environmental damage — what is it?
DDT: Organochloride known as an insecticide.
Sold under the brand name Valium, this benzodiazepine anxiolytic treats anxiety, seizures, alcohol withdrawal, and muscle spasms — and can even induce memory loss during procedures; what is it?
Diazepam: Benzodiazepine sedative. Diazepam, sold under the brand name Valium among others, is a medication of the benzodiazepine family that acts as an anxiolytic.
Marketed as Cymbalta, this serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor treats depression, anxiety, and fibromyalgia pain — what is it?
Born in Pretoria and once a Zip2 co-founder, this CEO of Tesla and SpaceX became, by some estimates, the first dollar trillionaire in 2026 — who is he?
Elon Musk: Businessman and public official (born 1971)
Also called moral philosophy, this field splits into normative, applied, and meta- branches as it asks what people ought to do and whether objective moral facts even exist. Which discipline is it?
Birds of prey in the genus Falco, some small species are called hobbies and hover-hunters are called kestrels — what are they collectively known as?
Falcon: Birds of prey in the genus Falco. The largest falcon is the gyrfalcon at up to 65 cm (26 in) in length.
Discovered in Dubna in 1999, this superheavy synthetic element (number 114) honors a Russian physicist whose name in Cyrillic explains why its spelling swaps a 'yo' for an 'e' — which element?
Flerovium: Chemical element with atomic number 114 (Fl)
Named in 1753 from Greek words for 'milk' and 'flower,' this genus of about 20 bulbous perennial species is better known by its common name, snowdrop — what is its scientific genus?
Galanthus: Genus of flowering plants in the family Amaryllidacee.

Likely first domesticated by Austronesian peoples in Maritime Southeast Asia, this herbaceous perennial is grown for the spicy rhizome that puts it in the same family as turmeric and cardamom — what is it?
Ginger: Species of plant used as a spice.
Standing up to a meter tall with a white head marked by a black stripe to its crest, this wading bird of Europe, Asia, and Africa hunts motionless beside water — what is it?
Grey heron: Long-legged predatory wading bird.
Powered by a Rolls-Royce Avon turbojet and featuring swept wings, this 1950s RAF fighter set a world air speed record of over 727 mph in September 1953 — which aircraft?
Hawker Hunter: 1950s family of British fighter aircraft.
Discovered in 1910 and stored in mast cells and basophils, this compound triggers immune responses and doubles as a neurotransmitter in the brain, spinal cord, and uterus — what is it?
Histamine: Organic compound involved in immune responses.
This nearly worldwide genus of flowering plants — commonly called St. John's wort — was the subject of a definitive taxonomic monograph identifying 36 sections within it. Which genus?
Hypericum: Genus of flowering plants known as St. John's worts.
Endemic to semiarid central-eastern Australia and also called the "fierce snake," this elapid was rediscovered in 1972 after nearly 90 years of obscurity — what is it?
Inland taipan: Extremely venomous snake native to Australia.
The first woman to chair the Federal Reserve, this American economist later became the first woman to serve as U.S. Treasury secretary — who is she?
Janet Yellen: American economist and government official (born 1946)
Also known as the English or Persian walnut, this tree species native to Eurasia is cultivated worldwide, with China as its leading producer today — what is it?
Juglans regia: Species of tree (walnut). Juglans regia, known by various common names including the common walnut, English walnut, or Persian walnut amongst other names, is a species of walnut.
This severe form of childhood protein malnutrition causes swelling and an enlarged, fatty liver, and is distinct from the calorie-deficient condition known as marasmus — what is it?
Kwashiorkor: Severe protein malnutrition. Kwashiorkor ( KWOSH-ee-OR-kor, -⁠kər) is a form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema and an enlarged liver with fatty infiltrates.
Sold under the brand name Xyzal, this less-sedating second-generation antihistamine for hay fever and hives was patented in 1965 but not approved in the US until 2007 — what is it?
Levocetirizine: Antihistamine medication. It is classified as a second-generation antihistamine and works by blocking histamine H1-receptors.
Sometimes called the Japanese medlar or Japanese plum, this evergreen tree from the hills of south-central China produces small orange fruit — which plant?
Loquat: Species of plant. The loquat (Eriobotrya japonica, Chinese: 枇杷; Pinyin: pípá) is a large evergreen shrub or tree grown commercially for its orange coloured fruits.
Genetically related to the Bichon, Bolognese, and Havanese, this toy breed sports a silky white coat, doesn't shed, and tops out around 4 kilograms — what breed is it?
Maltese dog: Breed of toy dog. The precise link, if any, between the modern and ancient breeds is not known.

The largest trijet ever built, this American wide-body airliner first flew in January 1990 and entered service with Finnair that December, a stretched, winglet-equipped update of an earlier trijet — what is it?
McDonnell Douglas MD-11: Wide body airliners developed from the DC-10.
Despite little formal schooling, this self-taught English scientist uncovered the principles behind electromagnetic induction and established the concept of the electromagnetic field — who is he?
Michael Faraday: English chemist and physicist (1791–1867)
Originally a dry-season staple for ǃKung hunter-gatherers, this tropical vine in the Cucurbitaceae family produces an intensely bitter edible fruit widely used across Asian cuisine — what is it?
Momordica charantia: Species of plant in the gourd family.
Found in cardiac and skeletal muscle and distantly related to hemoglobin, high levels of this oxygen-storing protein let diving whales and seals hold their breath longer — which protein?
Also known as black cumin or kalonji, this flowering plant native to the Levant and Iran is used across the world as a culinary spice — which species is it?
Nigella sativa: Species of flowering plant in the buttercup family.
Sold under the brand name Zyprexa, this atypical antipsychotic treats schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, and is sometimes used off-label to fight chemotherapy-induced nausea — what is this drug?
Olanzapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Olanzapine, sold under the brand name Zyprexa among others, is an atypical antipsychotic primarily used to treat schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
A pale-blue gas with a chlorine-like pungent odour, this unstable three-atom cousin of oxygen forms by UV light and electrical discharges and shields us high in the stratosphere — what is it?
This thick, fan-shaped muscle underlies the breast and is responsible for flexing, adducting, and internally rotating the upper arm — which chest muscle?
Pectoralis major: Main human chest muscle.

Nicknamed 'terror birds,' this family of large, mostly flightless carnivores roamed the Americas from the Cenozoic era, with one genus, Titanis, reaching as far as the southern United States — which family?
Phorusrhacidae: Extinct family of flightless birds. The exact number of genera is uncertain, as some taxa such as Brontornis may be different forms of bird instead.
Named after the American diplomat who introduced it from Mexico, this red-and-green Christmas plant is not actually toxic to pets — which plant?

Derived from arachidonic acid and containing a distinctive 5-carbon ring among its 20 carbons, this lipid compound can trigger opposite effects in different body tissues. What hormone-like substance is it?
Prostaglandin: Group of physiologically active lipid compounds.
Its thick bark gets harvested every 9 to 12 years for wine-bottle stoppers and cricket-ball cores — what species of oak, native to southwest Europe and Africa, is this?
Quercus suber: Species of plant. Quercus suber, commonly called the cork oak, is a medium-sized, evergreen oak tree in the section Quercus sect.

This dimensionless ratio of inertial to viscous forces predicts whether fluid flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent, and is used everywhere from pipe flow to aircraft wings — what is it?
Reynolds number: Ratio of inertial to viscous forces acting on a liquid.
Native to Eurasia and commonly known simply as the raspberry, this red-fruited bramble is widely cultivated across temperate regions — what species is it?
Typically emerging in young adulthood with hallucinations and delusions, this disorder has no objective lab test and needs symptoms for at least six months under the DSM-5 — what is it?
Schizophrenia: Mental disorder with psychotic symptoms.
Called the 'father of modern differential geometry,' this Chinese-born American mathematician and poet was honored with a medal the IMU named after him in 2010 — who is he?

Shiing-Shen Chern: Chinese-American mathematician and poet. Shiing-Shen Chern (Chinese: 陳省身; pinyin: Chén Xǐngshēn; October 26, 1911 – December 3, 2004) was a Chinese-born American mathematician and poet.

Native to Eurasia and found in Paleolithic-era deposits in ancient Britain, this flowering plant's ripe berries and cooked leaves are eaten in some regions despite its nightshade family's fearsome reputation — what is it?
Solanum nigrum: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family. The plant was known and mentioned by ancient herbalists, including Dioscorides.
This Taiwanese-American engineer co-founded YouTube and served as its CTO before later building the video app MixBit — who is he?
Also called the Java plum, this fast-growing evergreen tree from the Indian subcontinent can top 30 meters and live for over a century — which tree?
Syzygium cumini: Species of tree. It can reach heights of up to 30 m (100 ft) and can live more than 100 years.
Found in pufferfish, blue-ringed octopuses, and rough-skinned newts, this potent sodium-channel-blocking neurotoxin is also being trialed as a treatment for cancer-related pain — what is it?
Tetrodotoxin: Neurotoxin. Its name derives from Tetraodontiformes, an order that includes pufferfish, porcupinefish, ocean sunfish, and triggerfish; several of these species carry the toxin.
Nocturnal and tree-dwelling, this lizard species is native to Asia and various Pacific Islands — which reptile is it?
Tokay gecko: Species of reptile. The tokay gecko (Gekko gecko) is a nocturnal arboreal gecko in the genus Gekko, the true geckos.
Carrying the NATO nickname 'Backfire,' this supersonic Soviet bomber with variable-sweep wings first dropped conventional bombs during the Soviet–Afghan War — which aircraft is it?
Tupolev Tu-22M: Russian long-range supersonic strategic bomber.
Born in 1946, this German facilitator and non-fiction writer built a career exploring esoteric subjects until her death in 2011 — who was she?
Vera F. Birkenbihl: German facilitator, writer. Vera Felicitas Birkenbihl (26 April 1946 - 3 December 2011) was a German facilitator, non-fiction writer, and esoteric.
First isolated in 1669 by alchemist Henning Brand, this waxy, translucent form of an element glows faintly green in the dark and ignites spontaneously in air — which substance?
Sold under the brand name Ambien, which nonbenzodiazepine 'Z-drug' cuts the time to fall asleep by about fifteen minutes?
The symbol for scandium is Sc. Scandium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sc and atomic number 21.
The symbol for hydrogen is H. Hydrogen is a chemical element; it has the symbol H and atomic number 1.
